release_name: Revert diagnostic: restore standalone (Chrome was the real cause)
notes: Reverts v27.6.5. Real-device testing established that Chrome is Louis default browser on iOS, so every previous test in this investigation - the Add to Home Screen attempts, the fresh reinstall, the plain browser tab that appeared to work - was silently happening inside Chrome, not Safari, because iOS routes every link tap through the default browser invisibly. The share sheet that looked like Safari (AirDrop, Copy, Add to Reading List) is actually Apple own system-level share sheet, shared by every app, so it never actually indicated which browser was in use. Chrome for iOS cannot create a true installed web app the way Safari can - Apple restricts that capability to Safari - so a Chrome Add to Home Screen shortcut very likely does not even read the manifest display field at all, meaning the v27.6.5 minimal-ui change was solving a problem that was never actually confirmed to exist in genuine Safari. Reverted to standalone so the next real-device test (via the actual Safari app, deliberately, not a tapped link) is a clean test of whether Safari standalone mode ever had this problem in the first place, rather than a test muddied by an untested code change.
